_what_this_is: A one-off concept spec for ONE district: Copper Row, the market quarter, on Weighhouse Lane. Four items, two framings by two seeds each, so that what the prompt asked for can be told apart from what one seed happened to give. It is NOT an addition to the shipped library: it lives in its own file with its own out: line, because an item added to prompts.json is regenerated by every later night and lands in the shipped decals directory.

No file carrying Codex-authored prompt text was opened by the session that wrote it: not tools/imagegen/compare-hook-2026-09-09-pass2.json, not compare-hook-2026-09-09.json, not concept-prompts.json, concept-edit-prompts.json, concept-final-prompts.json, concept-period-prompts.json or pilot-image-inputs.json, none of which exist on disk beyond the two compare-hook files, and not the manifest.json or made.json under production/art/compare/, which embed a run's composed prompts. content_rules._provenance: NOT-MINE. Both values below are verbatim from tools/imagegen/prompts.json content_rules, which first landed 2026-08-25 in commit c7c20fbf. build_prompt refuses any prompt whose rules_clause lacks the words 'no trade marks', and appends it to every positive prompt. It is the one exclusion clause allowed in a positive prompt, and scan_exclusions exempts it by identity and prints that it did, because at cfg 1.0 the negative prompt is never encoded and moving it there would delete the only anti-brand instruction the model receives.
content_rules.rules_clause: invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness

style._framing_note: framing_required is the clause build_prompt refuses to ship a prompt without, and it checks the PREFIX rather than the composed text. For a texture plate that clause asks for a flat square-on surface. For a district sheet the hazard is different and is the one this clause is written against: a prompt that says sheet comes back as a grid of thumbnails or a painted board of vignettes, which is an illustration of a place rather than a photograph of one. So the clause asserts one frame, one viewpoint, one place, at standing height. Written fresh for this spec.
style.framing_required: a single continuous photograph of one real place, one frame and one viewpoint, taken at standing eye level
style.prefix: colour photograph on 35mm film, a single continuous photograph of one real place, one frame and one viewpoint, taken at standing eye level, 28mm lens, the camera 1.6m above the pavement, deep focus from the kerb to the far end of the street
style.suffix: a wet overcast November morning under low grey cloud, flat diffuse daylight, fine drizzle in the air, standing water in the gutter and rain sheen on the granite setts, soot and coal smuts dark on the brickwork, paint chalky and flaking, period colour print stock with cool green shadows and grain through the midtones, photoreal, grimy, lived in, late-analog Britain

defaults._note: steps 8 is the step count the tool's own cost anchors were measured at (COST_ANCHORS, RX 6700 / Vulkan / Z-Image-Turbo Q4_K / 8 steps, 25 Aug), so the estimate below is an estimate of the run this file actually asks for. cfg stays at 1.0 because the model is distilled for it: negative_state reports that at cfg 1.0 sd-cli never evaluates the unconditional branch, so every negative prompt in this file is RECORDED BUT INERT and the positive half carries the whole picture. That is not a reason to delete the negatives, it is the reason nothing load-bearing is in them.

negatives._note: VETOES ONLY, and inert at cfg 1.0 (see defaults). A negative vetoes but cannot summon: the Hook sheet's negative named pleasure marina and yacht and the picture still came back a pleasant basin, because a veto cannot put the trawlers in. So every element that must appear is in the positive half of each item and this list carries nothing the picture needs. Nouns, never phrases with an exclusion word in them: a negative prompt is a list of things to push away, so 'no people' in it asks the model to push away the phrase rather than the people.

_lettering.why_so_few: The measured record is that every extra lettering string degrades the lettering that already works, so the two canon anchors are spread across two framings rather than crowded into one. Both are canon rather than decoration: canon.md line 13 mints Weighhouse Lane and line 15 puts it in Copper Row; line 26 mints SNIDE as the Copper Row tag.
dropped_on_purpose: a 1871 date stone on the weighhouse, which would have been a third string in item 3 for a fact canon does not own

the line hand marked in marker on the Argus vendor board, which the brand bible describes and which would have been a second string in item 1; the board is asked for as an object and its words are left to the reviewer to reject
a shop fascia name, which would have needed the brand bible to mint a Copper Row trader first

_marks_owed_and_this_is_a_review_item: canon.md lines 74 to 77 record that the brand bible still owes the telephone operator's mark and kiosk lettering and the postal cypher on the pillar box. So the kiosk in item 1 and 2 is asked for as a red telephone kiosk and nothing more, and no pillar box is asked for at all. If the model paints a mark or a cypher on the kiosk anyway, that is a REFUSAL at review, not a pass: every image in a manifest is review=pending until a human has looked for anything resembling a real mark or a real face.

_provenance.research_cited_and_deliberately_unused: production/art/atlas-02/research/transport-timetables.md section 1 is CITED and says that after the Transport Act 1985 a 1990 town has competing liveries at the same stop and minibuses where double-deckers ran. No bus is asked for in either framing: a seven metre lane full of stalls is the wrong place for one, and an extra vehicle would dilute a prompt that is already carrying a market. Named here so nobody reads its absence as an oversight.
